title: First-pullback quality
statement: A high-quality first pullback follows a strong impulse, generally retraces no more than about 50%, shows lighter selling volume than buying volume, stays above VWAP and the 9 EMA, and avoids major topping-tail rejection.

evidence.title: Growing a $2k Account to $65,662.04 in 30 Days (My Day Trading Strategy)
evidence.note: The August course explicitly teaches <=50% retracement, lighter red volume, VWAP/9EMA support and topping-tail caution.

title: First candle to make a new high
statement: The canonical confirmation entry triggers as the first candle in the pullback breaks above the high of the preceding candle; it does not wait for that candle to close.

evidence.title: How To Start Day Trading in 2026 (full training)
evidence.note: The full training defines the first candle to make a new high as the entry.

title: Pullback-low invalidation
statement: The logical maximum loss for the canonical pullback entry is the low of the pullback.

evidence.title: How To Start Day Trading in 2026 (full training)
evidence.note: The full training places max loss at the pullback low.

title: Two-R opportunity to prior high
statement: For the canonical slower pullback entry, the distance to the prior/high-of-day target should plausibly provide about 2R relative to pullback-low risk.
implementation_notes: Do not automatically apply this exact prior-high target test to an advanced continuation entry that is intentionally taken at or above the former high; that is a separate setup family.

evidence.title: How To Start Day Trading in 2026 (full training)
evidence.note: The full training uses a retest of high-of-day and requires roughly twice the planned risk.

title: Micro pullback is a compressed fast-timeframe pullback
statement: A micro pullback is the compressed version of the pullback setup used when a fast stock does not provide a proper slower pullback. It may be a single pullback candle in the simple beginner formulation or several candles on a faster chart such as 10 seconds.
contradictions_or_exceptions: The January small-account lesson describes the simple micro pullback as one pullback candle, while the April dedicated class explicitly demonstrates multi-candle pullbacks on a 10-second chart. MomentumBot therefore treats 'micro' as timeframe-relative rather than hard-coding one candle.

evidence.title: I Reset My Account to $2,000 (AGAIN) Robinhood Challenge Ep 1
evidence.note: The small-account lesson presents the simplest micro form as a one-candle pullback.

evidence.title: The Micro Pullback Trading Strategy (Small Account Challenge)
evidence.note: The dedicated class explains that fast stocks may never form a proper one-minute pullback and demonstrates the setup on a 10-second chart with more than one pullback candle.

title: Prefer early pullbacks
statement: First and early pullbacks are preferred; later pullbacks can remain tradable but generally become more extended and choppier.

evidence.title: How To Start Day Trading in 2026 (full training)
evidence.note: Current training calls the first pullback a pocket of consistency and notes later pullbacks get choppier.

title: Micro pullback retracement quality
statement: The dedicated micro-pullback teaching carries over the requirement that the pullback should not retrace more than roughly 50% of the initial momentum move.
implementation_notes: The source defines the rule but not a unique machine swing-origin algorithm. The impulse origin must therefore be isolated as a research translation and validated against labeled examples rather than optimized silently.

evidence.title: The Micro Pullback Trading Strategy (Small Account Challenge)
evidence.note: The dedicated class explicitly says the micro pullback, like a proper pullback, should hold the 50% retracement of the initial move.

title: Canonical micro confirmation trigger
statement: The canonical micro-pullback confirmation is the first fast-timeframe candle to make a new high over the preceding candle; entry occurs while the candle is forming rather than after its close.

evidence.title: Level 2 for Day Trading (+$65k in 2hrs After Spotting Hidden Buyers)
evidence.note: The Level-2 lesson calls first-candle-new-high the usual rule-of-thumb micro entry.

evidence.title: The Micro Pullback Trading Strategy (Small Account Challenge)
evidence.note: The dedicated class repeatedly demonstrates entry on the first candle to make a new high, including on the 10-second chart.

title: Hidden-buyer anticipation is an exception
statement: An experienced discretionary exception may anticipate the first-new-high trigger when Level 2 and tape show a very clear hidden/stacked buyer supporting the pullback; this is not part of the deterministic chart-only baseline.
implementation_notes: Requires historical quote/order-book/tape features or an AI context review. Do not proxy this by lowering the deterministic trigger price.

evidence.title: Level 2 for Day Trading (+$65k in 2hrs After Spotting Hidden Buyers)
evidence.note: Ross says he normally buys when the first candle makes a new high unless a very clear hidden buyer at support gives him reason to anticipate.

evidence.title: The Micro Pullback Trading Strategy (Small Account Challenge)
evidence.note: The AGPU case study describes buyers stacked at the $8 bid plus green time-and-sales prints as the reason to punch the trade around whole-dollar support.

title: Half-dollar and whole-dollar context
statement: Half-dollar and whole-dollar prices are recurring psychological support/resistance and continuation targets. They are context features, not by themselves sufficient entry signals.
implementation_notes: The canonical micro baseline may expose distance to the next half/whole dollar as a feature; anticipatory entries at those levels remain context-dependent until supported by market-microstructure data.

evidence.title: The Micro Pullback Trading Strategy (Small Account Challenge)
evidence.note: The dedicated class describes retest/continuation targets at the next half or whole dollar and notes buyers often support dips around those levels.

evidence.title: My Account Is Up Over 1,000% in 17 Days...
evidence.note: The VRAX recap describes taking a second micro-pullback continuation for a break of $6.

title: Use the faster chart when the slower pullback never forms
statement: On extremely fast momentum, a 10-second chart can be used to observe micro pullbacks that are invisible or compressed inside a one-minute candle; the slower one-minute strategy should not be loosened simply to manufacture those trades.

evidence.title: The Micro Pullback Trading Strategy (Small Account Challenge)
evidence.note: The dedicated class explicitly says waiting for a proper one-minute setup can leave the trader on the sidelines and demonstrates micro pullbacks on a 10-second chart.

evidence.title: My Account Is Up Over 1,000% in 17 Days...
evidence.note: The VRAX recap identifies the actual trade as a second micro pullback; reconstructed SIP data shows that sequence is compressed inside one consolidated one-minute bar.

title: Starter first trade / cushion
statement: Begin the session with a starter-sized first trade; if it works, the resulting cushion can justify greater aggression, while an immediate failure raises a caution flag.

evidence.title: Top 5 Reasons Why Traders Lose Money 💰Don’t Make These Mistakes!!!
evidence.note: Ross explicitly describes using a starter on the first trade to test the water and only gaining confidence after a successful first trade.

title: No averaging down
statement: Do not add to a losing position in the baseline.

evidence.title: How I Made $500,000 in 7 Days of Day Trading (Full Training)
evidence.note: The full training explicitly states do not average down and defines it as adding to losing trades.

title: Slippage can invalidate entry
statement: If actual entry slippage materially increases stop distance and destroys the required reward/risk, exit or reject rather than pretending the original plan still applies.

evidence.title: My Account Is Up Over 1,000% in 17 Days...
evidence.note: A current recap explains that roughly 15-20 cents of entry slippage materially increased planned risk and made the original reward/risk much worse.
